description: Capability self-awareness and thinking upgrade for Claude. One front door (scripts/hub.py find) maps a task in the user's words to the runnable tools, catalog powers and guides that fit, and says what this machine can run now. Covers what Claude can do in the current session (tools, connectors, installable libraries, surfaces), how to think, create and verify better, and a searchable catalog of 4,700+ powers in 10 domains (thinking, writing and Arabic, code, data, documents, research, apps, image and audio, product and finance, motion graphics and video), each with requirements, an evidence badge and proofs. Use at the start of any substantial or creative task, when asked what Claude can do, told to use its superpowers, or given this skill's repository link; and for motion graphics, montage, captions, reels, video edits, drawing, 3D, image design and lawful software investigation. tools.summary_en: Reports what each catalog power needs (tools, pip/npm packages, keys, platforms, fonts, models), which of those this machine has, and the install commands for the powers suggested for a task. Maintainer subcommands re-derive the `requires` fields and regenerate references/requirements.md.
tools.summary_ar: يبيّن ما تحتاجه كل قدرة في الكتالوج من أدوات وحزم pip وnpm ومفاتيح ومنصات وخطوط ونماذج، وما المتوفر منها على هذا الجهاز، وأوامر التثبيت للقدرات المقترحة لمهمة ما. وتعيد أوامر الصيانة اشتقاق حقول requires وتوليد الملف references/requirements.md.
use_when: ايش لازم أثبت عشان أسوي ريلز بتعليق صوتي وترجمة متزامنة؟
القدرة GLOW-05 محتاجة ايه عشان تشتغل؟
What do I need to install before starting this task?
Which registered requirements are present on this machine?
Check that every power's requires field is up to date

commands.name: present
commands.does: Marks every registered requirement present, missing or unknown on this machine (read-only, about 1 s)

commands.name: for
commands.does: Checklist for one power: each requirement's state, kind and install command

commands.name: plan
commands.example: python3 scripts/requirements.py plan "Arabic reel with voice-over and synced captions" --limit 8 --json
commands.does: Suggests powers for a task, then merges their requirements into one checklist with install commands; ▶ marks powers whose requirements are all present

commands.name: derive-check
commands.does: Exits 1 if re-deriving `requires` from install/how text would change any record; read-only

commands.name: derive
commands.does: Rewrites the `requires` field in data/powers/*.json from the patterns in data/requirements.json

commands.name: index
commands.does: Regenerates references/requirements.md (requirement to powers unlocked); --probe adds present/missing marks for this machine

tools.inputs: A power id (for), a task sentence (plan, with --limit and --json), or nothing (present, derive, index). Reads data/requirements.json, data/powers/*.json and environment-variable names.
tools.outputs: Checklists with 🟢/📦/🔑/❔ marks and install commands, or JSON (plan --json, present --json), on stdout. derive rewrites data/powers/*.json; index rewrites references/requirements.md; derive --check exits 1 when stale.
tools.consent: `derive` (without --check) rewrites data/powers/*.json and `index` rewrites references/requirements.md inside the skill; both are maintainer actions. The install commands it prints need user approval before anyone runs them, especially paid or system-wide installs.
tools.limits: It detects presence only (shutil.which, importlib find_spec, env-var name set, font file exists), never version fit or output quality, and it treats a power with no listed requirement as ready.
tools.evidence_note: 6/6 passed (python3 -m unittest tests.test_requirements)

tools.summary_en: Maps a task to an ordered set of the 15 vendored obra/superpowers v7 process skills (brainstorming, debugging, TDD, verification and others), checks the vendored sources, and can install KOSIF plus those skills into ~/.claude/skills with backups.
tools.summary_ar: يربط المهمة بمجموعة مرتبة من مهارات العمل الخمس عشرة المضمّنة من obra/superpowers الإصدار 7 (مثل العصف الذهني وتتبّع الأخطاء والتطوير المقاد بالاختبارات والتحقق)، ويفحص المصادر المضمّنة، ويستطيع تثبيت KOSIF مع تلك المهارات في ‎~/.claude/skills مع نسخ احتياطية.
use_when: أي مهارات عمل أستخدمها لإصلاح عطل في التطبيق؟
اعمل خطة لتطوير برنامج المونتاج، أي منهجية أتبع؟
Which process skills apply to 'Fix the crash in the montage app'?
Install KOSIF Superpowers and the obra process skills into my Claude skills folder
Check whether the vendored superpowers skills are complete

commands.name: doctor
commands.does: Checks the vendored MIT LICENSE and the 15 process SKILL.md files, and reports how many are installed under ~/.claude/skills. Exits with code 2 if sources are missing.

commands.name: plan
commands.example: python3 scripts/superpowers_unified.py plan "Fix the crash in the montage app"
commands.does: Uses a fixed keyword table to return an ordered list of process skills, starting with using-superpowers and ending with verification-before-completion.

commands.name: list
commands.does: Lists the 15 vendored process-skill names.

commands.name: install
commands.does: Copies kosif-superpowers and the 15 process skills into ~/.claude/skills and skips existing ones unless --force is given (existing copies are backed up to ~/.claude/backups/kosif-ultimate-<UTC stamp>). Without --no-global-instructions it also appends a policy block to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md.

tools.inputs: A task text for plan. It reads vendor/obra-superpowers-v7/skills/*/SKILL.md and LICENSE. install targets the user's home directory (~/.claude).
tools.outputs: JSON on stdout. install also writes ~/.claude/skills/<name>/, ~/.claude/backups/kosif-ultimate-<stamp>/ and, optionally, ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md.
tools.consent: install writes outside the repository: it copies 16 skill folders into ~/.claude/skills, replaces existing ones with --force (after backing them up), and appends to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md unless --no-global-instructions is given. Get explicit user approval before running install. doctor, plan and list are read-only.
tools.limits: plan is a fixed keyword-to-skill lookup and doctor checks only that files exist; neither one runs, verifies or tests any skill.
tools.evidence_note: 7/7 passed (install was exercised in a temporary home directory)

tools.title_ar: بوابة حفظ الحقائق عند إعادة الصياغة
tools.summary_en: Compares a text before and after a rewrite (English and Arabic) and reports any factual anchor that was dropped or added: quotes, numbers, currencies, dates, months, weekdays, emails, URLs, paths, handles, versions, ratios and must-keep names. It returns PASS or REVIEW_REQUIRED.
tools.summary_ar: يقارن النص قبل إعادة الصياغة وبعدها (بالعربية والإنجليزية) ويعرض كل مرتكز حقائقي حُذف أو أُضيف، مثل الاقتباسات والأرقام والعملات والتواريخ والشهور وأيام الأسبوع والبريد والروابط والمسارات والحسابات والإصدارات والنسب والأسماء الواجب بقاؤها، ثم يعطي النتيجة PASS أو REVIEW_REQUIRED.
use_when: اتأكد إن إعادة الصياغة ما غيرتش أي رقم أو اسم أو تاريخ
تحقق أن البرومبت المحسّن ما ضيّع تفاصيل طلبي الأصلي
قارن النص الأصلي بالنسخة المعدلة وقل لي وش انحذف من الحقائق
check that my rewrite kept every number, name and link
verify the optimized prompt didn't drop any of the user's details
gate a humanized draft so no facts were invented or lost

commands.name: rewrite (files)
commands.does: Default rewrite mode: PASS only if nothing was dropped and nothing was added. --text prints a one-line summary instead of JSON. Exits 0 on PASS, 2 on REVIEW_REQUIRED.

commands.name: --keep (must-keep names file)
commands.does: Adds terms (one per line) that must survive; they are counted by presence, not by count. Prints the JSON report.

commands.name: inline text + --keep-term
commands.example: python3 scripts/anchor_gate.py --before-text "قابلنا أحمد يوم الخميس" --after-text "قابلنا محمود يوم الجمعة" --keep-term أحمد --text
commands.does: Compares inline strings; --keep-term can be repeated.

commands.name: --mode prompt
commands.does: Prompt mode: PASS when nothing was dropped; additions are listed for review (for checking an optimized prompt against the user's raw prompt).

commands.name: stdin
commands.does: Reads one side from stdin ('-'); only one side may come from stdin.

tools.inputs: Exactly one of --before/--before-text and one of --after/--after-text (UTF-8 files up to 5 MB, or '-' for stdin on one side), plus an optional --keep file and repeatable --keep-term.
tools.outputs: JSON (status, mode, dropped, added, kept, note) or a one-line --text summary on stdout. Exit 0 PASS, 2 REVIEW_REQUIRED, 64 usage error.
tools.limits: It only checks that surface anchors survived, so a PASS does not prove that meaning, tone, attribution or unlisted names were preserved.
tools.evidence_note: 62/62 checks passed, shared with tell_scan (python3 -I proofs/general-writing/test_writing.py; includes CLI exit codes 0/2/64)

tools.summary_en: Computes a deterministic back-of-envelope capacity estimate (average and peak RPS, minimum replicas, logical and replicated storage in bytes and GiB) from caller-supplied traffic and hardware assumptions, using exact decimal arithmetic.
tools.summary_ar: يحسب تقديرًا تقريبيًا وحتميًا لسعة النظام (متوسط الطلبات في الثانية وذروتها، والحد الأدنى من النسخ، والتخزين المنطقي والمكرر بالبايت والجيبيبايت) من افتراضات المرور والعتاد التي يقدّمها المستخدم، بحساب عشري دقيق.
use_when: احسب لي كم سيرفر محتاج لو عندي مليون طلب في اليوم
قدّر مساحة التخزين المطلوبة لمدة الاحتفاظ دي
كم نسخة نحتاج للخدمة وقت الذروة؟
estimate replicas and storage for 10M requests per day
do a back-of-envelope system design sizing
how much storage for 30-day retention with 2 copies

commands.name: size
commands.does: Prints JSON with average_rps, peak_rps, peak_rps_ceiling, minimum_replicas, logical_storage_bytes, retained_storage_bytes, storage_gib, assumptions and the list of exclusions.

tools.inputs: Six required numeric assumptions: --daily-requests, --peak-factor (>=1), --payload-bytes, --retention-days, --replica-rps and --target-utilization (0-1], plus optional --copies (a positive integer, default 1).
tools.outputs: JSON on stdout (status deterministic_estimate_not_load_test, executed_benchmark false). It exits 2 with an argparse error on missing or out-of-range inputs.
tools.limits: Linear arithmetic on assumed numbers only; it runs no load test and excludes indexes, caching, backups, compression, burst shape, network, CDN, failover headroom and regional placement.
tools.evidence_note: 9/9 ArchitectureSizerTests passed (file total 15/15 including python_package_probe tests)

tools.summary_en: Turns one problem statement into a reproducible, ranked JSON list of falsifiable engineering ideas (16 inventive methods × 4 lenses), each with a hypothesis, test, success metric and rejection threshold.
tools.summary_ar: يحوّل وصف مشكلة واحدة إلى قائمة JSON مرتّبة وقابلة لإعادة الإنتاج من أفكار هندسية قابلة للتفنيد (16 طريقة ابتكار × 4 زوايا)، لكل فكرة فرضية واختبار ومقياس نجاح وحدّ رفض.
use_when: اقترح لي حلول مبتكرة لمشكلة بطء الترجمة على الموبايل
عايز أفكار جديدة لتحسين الأداة دي مع معايير نجاح واضحة
ابغى أفكار هندسية قابلة للاختبار لمشكلة عندي
brainstorm falsifiable engineering alternatives for this bottleneck
invent options to make our render pipeline more resilient
give me TRIZ-style ideas with kill criteria

commands.name: methods
commands.does: Prints the 16 inventive methods (technique + suggested experiment) as JSON.

commands.name: invent
commands.example: python3 scripts/invention_lab.py invent "Make Arabic captions render faster on mobile" --count 12 --constraint "no paid APIs"
commands.does: Prints schema kosif-invention-candidates-v1 JSON with up to --count (1-64) candidates sorted by a deterministic heuristic priority; each --constraint (repeatable) is echoed into every candidate's risk field.

tools.inputs: A problem statement of 8-2000 characters (positional), optional --count 1-64 (default 12) and repeatable --constraint strings.
tools.outputs: JSON on stdout (schema kosif-invention-candidates-v1): problem, constraints, disclaimer and candidates with id, method, lens, proposal, hypothesis, test, success_metric, failure_threshold, novelty_status, risk, cost_class, priority_score.
tools.limits: Fills fixed templates from a problem string and ranks them by a SHA-256-seeded heuristic, so it gives no real novelty, feasibility, cost or patent assessment.
tools.evidence_note: 4/4 passed (python3 -m unittest tests.test_invention_lab)

tools.summary_en: Scans English and Arabic (MSA and Egyptian) prose for stock 'AI-sounding' writing habits and tool leftovers, and reports each hit with its line, strength and an overall verdict (EDIT/REVIEW/LOOK/LEAVE/CLEAN).
tools.summary_ar: يفحص النصوص الإنجليزية والعربية (الفصحى والمصرية) بحثًا عن العبارات النمطية التي تبدو آلية وبقايا أدوات التوليد، ويعرض كل إشارة مع رقم سطرها وقوتها وحكمًا عامًا على النص (EDIT/REVIEW/LOOK/LEAVE/CLEAN).
use_when: الكلام ده باين عليه مكتوب بالذكاء الاصطناعي؟ افحصه
راجع المقال وطلّع العبارات الآلية قبل ما أنشره
أبغى أعرف وش الجمل اللي تحتاج إعادة صياغة في المسودة
scan this draft for AI writing tells before I publish
check my LinkedIn post for chatbot phrases
make CI fail if the reply text has strong AI tells

commands.name: scan
commands.does: Prints a human report per file: verdict, word and sentence stats, then each hit (strength, rule id, line, label, matched text), strongest first.

commands.name: scan --json
commands.does: Prints a machine-readable JSON report (a list when several files are given) with verdict, families, hits and rhythm stats.

commands.name: stdin
commands.does: Scans text piped on stdin ('-').

commands.name: --fail-on
commands.does: Exits 1 when any file's verdict is at or above the given level (edit, review or look); useful as a gate.

commands.name: --include-code / --include-quotes
commands.does: Also scans fenced/inline code, URLs and blockquotes, and the inside of quotations (all masked by default).

commands.name: --list-rules
commands.does: Prints every rule id (H1..H25, X1, AR1..AR26 and computed rules), its strength and label, then exits.

tools.inputs: One or more UTF-8 text or Markdown files, or '-' for stdin.
tools.outputs: Human-readable report or JSON on stdout (verdict, verdict_text, words, sentences, mean_sentence_words, sentence_length_stdev, tells_per_100_words, families, hits with id/strength/label/line/match); exit 1 with --fail-on when the threshold is reached.
tools.limits: A regex-based editing aid that shows where to look; it is not an authorship or AI detector, and it never rewrites text or judges meaning.
tools.evidence_note: 62/62 checks passed, shared with anchor_gate (python3 -I proofs/general-writing/test_writing.py; this is a script-style regression runner, not unittest)

tools.summary_en: Turns thinking procedures into checkable text scaffolds. It picks a reasoning level (L0–L6), writes a task contract, ranks 63 mental models, drafts a backcast plan, builds an idea matrix from catalog powers, scores a weighted decision with sensitivity, runs a Monte-Carlo Fermi estimate and flags weak wording in a draft.
tools.summary_ar: يحوّل إجراءات التفكير إلى قوالب نصية قابلة للفحص. يختار مستوى التفكير (L0–L6)، ويكتب عقد المهمة، ويرتّب 63 نموذجًا ذهنيًا، ويصوغ خطة بالتخطيط العكسي، ويبني مصفوفة أفكار من قدرات الكتالوج، ويقيّم قرارًا موزونًا مع اختبار الحساسية، ويجري تقدير فيرمي بطريقة مونت كارلو، ويرصد الصياغات الضعيفة في المسودة.
use_when: فكّر بعمق في المهمة دي قبل ما تبدأ
اعطني أفكار مبتكرة لريل الجمعة
Which option should I choose? Run a weighted decision with sensitivity
Estimate the range for users × conversion × price
راجع المسودة وطلّع لي العبارات المبالغ فيها
Plan the course launch over 6 weeks

commands.name: ladder
commands.example: python3 scripts/think.py ladder "design a 30-day plan for a course launch"
commands.does: Picks the reasoning level L0–L6 from keywords (default L2; tasks over 25 words go to at least L4), prints its steps, and from L4 up the models worth running

commands.name: frame
commands.example: python3 scripts/think.py frame "a 15 s reel at 30 fps"
commands.does: Prints a contract template: goal, reader, done-criteria, constraints (numbers pulled from the task), non-goals, unknowns, first probe

commands.name: models
commands.example: python3 scripts/think.py models "pricing a new subscription" -n 3 --json
commands.does: Ranks mental models from data/mental_models.json and prints each one's question, steps, output and pitfall

commands.name: plan
commands.does: Backcast plan template: end state, week milestones, WBS skeleton, critical path, pre-mortem, kill criteria

commands.name: ideas
commands.does: Idea matrix: creative operators paired with nearby and far-domain catalog powers, with each power's requirements

commands.name: decide
commands.does: Weighted decision matrix; JSON with totals, winner, margin, robust, and the flips under a ±1 weight change

commands.name: fermi
commands.example: python3 scripts/think.py fermi "a*b*c" --range a=1:3 b=10:20 c=0.1:0.3 --samples 2000
commands.does: Monte-Carlo range (log-uniform when lo>0) for an arithmetic factor tree; JSON with p10, p50, p90 and mean

commands.name: critic
commands.does: Flags intensifiers, unverified claims, absolutes, vague lists, AI-tell words and bare completion claims, with file:line, and counts the digits in the text

tools.inputs: A task, problem, goal or seed sentence. decide takes a JSON file {"criteria": {name: weight}, "scores": {option: {criterion: score}}}. fermi takes an arithmetic expression plus --range name=lo:hi for every name. critic takes a text or Markdown file.
tools.outputs: Text templates on stdout (ladder, frame, plan, ideas, and critic flags), or JSON (models --json, decide, fermi). Nothing is written to disk.
tools.limits: It produces templates and keyword-based rankings to think with; the blanks (…) still have to be filled and tested, and it does not reason about or verify claims by itself.
tools.evidence_note: 9/9 passed (python3 -m unittest tests.test_think)

tools.summary_en: Stdlib Python module that turns any aspect spec (W:H ratio, WxH pixels, or an English/Arabic platform name such as reel, cinema or مربع) into a label and even pixel dimensions, plus ratio, resolution-string and validity helpers.
tools.summary_ar: وحدة بايثون من المكتبة القياسية تحوّل أي صيغة لنسبة العرض (نسبة W:H أو أبعاد WxH بالبكسل أو اسم منصة بالإنجليزية أو العربية مثل reel أو سينما أو مربع) إلى وسم وأبعاد بكسل زوجية، مع دوال للنسبة ونص الدقة والتحقق من الصحة.
use_when: What pixel size should a 2.35:1 cinema video be?
Resolve 'reel' or '21:9' to an even H.264-safe resolution
كم أبعاد فيديو مقاس سينمائي أو مربع؟
ابي أعرف الدقة المناسبة لمقاس تيك توك
Validate the aspect the user typed before scaffolding

commands.name: import
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); import aspects; print(aspects.resolve('2.35:1'))"
commands.does: Imports the module from the skill root; prints ('2.35:1', 1920, 818).

commands.name: resolve
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); from aspects import resolve; print(resolve('ريلز'))"
commands.does: Returns (label, width, height) with even dimensions; here ('9:16', 1080, 1920). Raises ValueError for unreadable specs or ratios outside 1:5–5:1.

commands.name: ratio_of
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); from aspects import ratio_of; print(ratio_of('1920x816'))"
commands.does: Returns width/height as a float for any accepted spec.

commands.name: resolution
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); from aspects import resolution; print(resolution('cinema'))"
commands.does: Returns a 'WxH' string; cinema -> 1920x804.

commands.name: is_valid
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); from aspects import is_valid; print(is_valid('foo'))"
commands.does: Returns True/False instead of raising.

tools.inputs: An aspect spec string: integer or decimal W:H (9:16, 2.35:1), explicit WxH pixels (1920x816), or a name (reel, story, tiktok, shorts, youtube, square, feed, portrait, classic, cinema, scope, ultrawide, flat, or Arabic names like ريلز، مربع، سينما).
tools.outputs: (label, width, height) tuple with even dimensions; float ratio; 'WxH' string; boolean validity.
tools.limits: Only maps aspect specs to even pixel sizes (1080 px short side or 1920 px long side, ratios 1:5–5:1); it does not resize, crop or reframe media.
tools.evidence_note: 4/4 passed (imports the byte-identical repo copy tools/aspects.py). Manually imported the skill copy and called resolve/ratio_of/resolution/is_valid: OK.

tools.summary_en: Turns a kosif.audio-cues.v1 JSON (measured onsets plus aligned words from audio_cue_mapper.py) into an editable motion_director storyboard with timed text, draw-on path, character and camera zoom, plus a decision report that scores the doodle, kinetic and cinematic styles.
tools.summary_ar: يحوّل ملف JSON بصيغة kosif.audio-cues.v1 (بدايات الأصوات المقيسة والكلمات المحاذاة من audio_cue_mapper.py) إلى لوحة قصة قابلة للتحرير بصيغة motion_director، فيها نص مؤقّت ومسار يُرسم تدريجيًا وشخصية وتقريب كاميرا، مع تقرير قرار يقيّم أساليب doodle وkinetic وcinematic.
use_when: حوّل التعليق الصوتي وتوقيت الكلمات لستوري بورد موشن جرافيك
اعمل لي مشاهد متزامنة مع الصوت من ملف cues.json
أبغى لوحة قصة رأسية للريلز مبنية على توقيت كلماتي
turn my audio cues and word timings into an editable motion storyboard
pick a doodle, kinetic or cinematic style for this voiceover and build scenes
generate a 9:16 scene plan synced to the narration

commands.name: plan (auto style)
commands.does: Validates the cues, scores the three styles with a declared heuristic, splits the audio into scenes of up to 9 s at word boundaries, and writes a new 1080x1920 30 fps storyboard JSON and a decision/evidence report. It prints a one-line JSON summary (rendered: false).

commands.name: plan (forced style, landscape)
commands.does: Uses the chosen style (doodle, kinetic or cinematic) and a 1920x1080 frame.

tools.inputs: A kosif.audio-cues.v1 JSON produced by scripts/audio_cue_mapper.py (duration 0.1-120 s, up to 600 onset candidates, up to 1,500 non-overlapping timed words), plus --out and --report paths that are new, distinct and inside existing directories.
tools.outputs: Two new JSON files: the storyboard (motion_director spec version 1, ready for 'motion_director.py compile') and the report (schema kosif.creative-plan.v1: decision with style scores, evidence, validated_storyboard, render_status unrendered_storyboard). A summary is printed to stdout.
tools.limits: Builds an unrendered storyboard from a hand-written style heuristic and amplitude onsets; it does not understand lyrics or emotion, verify beats, or render video.
tools.evidence_note: 6/6 passed

tools.summary_en: Validates a word-timed JSON scene script (paths, circles, text, characters, actors, morphs, camera) and compiles it into a self-contained seekable SVG/HTML animation, with an optional MP4 render through the bundled render_html.cjs.
tools.summary_ar: يتحقق من نص مشاهد بصيغة JSON مُوقَّت على مستوى الكلمات (مسارات ودوائر ونصوص وشخصيات وتحوّلات وحركة كاميرا) ثم يحوّله إلى رسم متحرك SVG/HTML مستقل قابل للتقديم إلى أي لحظة، مع إمكانية تصديره اختياريًا إلى MP4 عبر محرك العرض المرفق.
use_when: Turn my words.json timings into an animated SVG explainer
Compile this scene JSON into a seekable HTML animation and render it to MP4 with my voice
اعمل لي موشن جرافيك عربي متزامن مع الكلمات من ملف JSON
حوّل السكربت ده لأنيميشن رسم خطوط يتحرك مع الصوت
ابي فيديو رسم بالكود مقاس ريلز ٩:١٦ مع التعليق الصوتي

commands.name: doctor
commands.does: Probes for the motion engine asset, render_html.cjs, node, ffmpeg and ffprobe; renders nothing.

commands.name: sample
commands.does: Writes a valid 9-second, 3-scene 1080x1920 Arabic demo spec (refuses to overwrite an existing file).

commands.name: compile
commands.does: Validates the spec and writes a new self-contained HTML/SVG animation exposing window.__kosif.seek(t); status html_compiled_not_rendered.

commands.name: render
commands.does: Runs node render_html.cjs --mode seek --offline (Playwright Chromium + ffmpeg) to produce a new MP4, optionally muxing the user's audio; result is marked verified:false.

commands.name: import
commands.example: import {ease, interpolate, timeline, strokeReveal, camera, walkRig, parallax, seededSketchLine, timeCode, wordCueState, assertFrameContract, clamp} from "./resources/motion-runtime/motion_toolkit.mjs";
commands.does: Loads all 12 named exports in Node.js or an ES-module browser page. No npm packages are needed.

commands.name: ease
commands.example: ease(0.5, "cubic")  // 0.5; kinds: linear | smooth | in | out | cubic
commands.does: Clamps u to 0..1 and applies the named easing curve. Throws on an unknown kind.

commands.name: interpolate
commands.does: Eases from `from` to `to` between times a and b. Throws if b<=a or any value is non-finite.

commands.name: timeline
commands.does: Multi-keyframe track with held endpoints. Keyframe times must strictly increase.

commands.name: strokeReveal
commands.does: Returns dasharray/dashoffset values that draw an SVG path of the given length like a pen between start and end.

commands.name: camera
commands.does: Returns {zoom, x, y} for an eased zoom-about-centre plus pan.

commands.name: walkRig
commands.does: Returns leg and arm angles in degrees plus an `active` value that ramps in over 0.5 s after onset.

commands.name: parallax
commands.does: Scales the camera offset by a layer depth from 0 to 1.

commands.name: seededSketchLine
commands.does: Returns steps+1 jittered points that look hand-drawn. Endpoints are exact, and the same seed always gives the same line.

commands.name: timeCode
commands.does: Formats seconds as HH:MM:SS:FF at an integer fps from 1 to 240.

commands.name: wordCueState
commands.does: Returns per-word active/progress state for caption timing without splitting Arabic words.

commands.name: assertFrameContract
commands.does: Checks duration, fps and even width/height before rendering and returns the total frame count.

commands.name: clamp
commands.does: Clamps a number into [min, max], 0..1 by default.

tools.inputs: Plain numbers and objects passed as function arguments, such as time in seconds, keyframe arrays [{time, value}], word cues [{word, start, end}], and option objects.
tools.outputs: New plain values or objects (numbers, {strokeDasharray, strokeDashoffset}, {zoom, x, y}, point arrays, timecode strings). Invalid input throws an Error. No files are written.
tools.limits: Supplies math primitives only: it draws, renders and edits nothing, and has just five easing curves and a single sine-based walk cycle.

tools.summary_en: The skill's bundled copy of KOSIF's deterministic HTML-to-MP4 renderer. It renders a local or http HTML film frame by frame in headless Chromium, either through the page's window.__kosif.seek(t) or under Chromium virtual time for any CSS/WAAPI/rAF page. It encodes H.264 with ffmpeg, optionally muxes untouched audio, and checks fps, frame count, duration, size and audio with ffprobe. --preview makes an 8-frame contact sheet instead.

commands.name: render

commands.name: help
commands.does: Prints every option (--aspect, --width, --height, --fps, --duration, --start, --audio, --mode, --preview, --frames-dir, --keep-frames, --crf, --scale, --seed, --offline, --timeout, --settle) and the exit codes.

tools.inputs: A local .html file or an http(s) URL. In seek mode the page exposes window.__kosif = {duration, seek(t)} (and optionally window.__kosifReady); otherwise --duration is required. Optional audio file. Options: --aspect (9:16, 16:9, 4:5, 21:9, WxH or a name such as reel/square/cinema), fps, crf, scale, seed and others.
tools.outputs: An H.264 MP4 at --out (or <out-stem>_preview.png with --preview) and a VERIFY line with duration, fps, frames, size and audio. PNG frames go to --frames-dir if given, otherwise to a temp dir that is deleted. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 usage, 2 render/encode failure, 3 ffprobe mismatch.
tools.consent: An http(s) --in URL, or a page that loads remote assets, contacts the network (use --offline to block it). It runs the page's own scripts in headless Chromium, so render only pages the user trusts. It overwrites --out, and --frames-dir deletes existing frame_######.png and preview_*.png files in that folder.
tools.limits: Verifies only container metrics (fps, frame count, duration, size, audio presence), not visual or creative correctness. It needs Playwright Chromium and ffmpeg/ffprobe already installed and installs nothing.

tools.inputs: --words: a bare JSON array of {word|text,start,end,emphasis?} in seconds; --clips: JSON array of clips with id, path, duration, width, height, license_verified, reviewed_frames, contains_text, contains_excluded_people, is_moving_video, and tags/description; --duration: audio seconds; --fps: 24/25/30/60; --out: JSON path.

commands.name: paper-edit

commands.does: Converts [{time,comment,x?,y?}] notes into sorted markers (kosif.frame-review.v1), each with a stable 12-hex id, an exact frame, HH:MM:SS:FF timecode and an optional pixel point from normalized x/y.
